programme: TFDP1, MXD1, MAZ and PAX8 sit in the RB–E2F / MYC–MAX–MXD cell-cycle switch: TFDP1 is the obligate DP partner that lets E2F drive S-phase entry (its own target list is the E2F canon — CDK2, CDK4, RB1, MYC, PCNA, CCNA2, MYBL2); MXD1 is the MAX-network brake that normally terminates MYC-driven growth and forces differentiation; MAZ is a GC-box factor that reinforces transcription at many of the same proliferative promoters MYC/MAX occupy; PAX8's target set (E2F1, RB1, TP53, TERT) sits on the same checkpoint genes even though PAX8 itself is not gut/skin-lineage. TRIM28/KAP1 is the corepressor that restrains this network directly at E2F3/E2F4, and is the one factor with disease-specific documentation on both sides.
role_in_a: Not an established hyperproliferative axis in IBS the way it is in psoriasis. If active, it would show up as dysregulated cell-cycle re-entry during crypt/mucosal turnover and repair rather than as a named disease mechanism. The only direct evidence retrieved for this pair's IBS side (TRIM28, PMID 39936987) is about endogenous retrovirus derepression, not about the E2F/MYC–MAX arm specifically — so the cell-cycle role in IBS is inferred, not documented.
role_in_b: This is the textbook axis of psoriatic keratinocyte hyperproliferation: RB–E2F re-entry into S phase is what produces the epidermal thickening that defines a plaque. TRIM28 is directly documented here, promoting keratinocyte proliferation through an NLRP3/SGT1-linked route (PMID 42720284) — a concrete, disease-specific instance of this factor acting on the proliferative axis.
shared_axis: Both colonic and epidermal epithelia depend on RB–E2F/MYC–MAX control to balance proliferation against differentiation during routine turnover. If the same corepressor (TRIM28) and network components misfire in both tissues, the two diseases could converge on a de-repressed proliferative epithelial state even though the clinical readout differs — visible hyperplasia in skin versus altered regenerative/barrier turnover in gut.
reasoning: The RB–E2F/MYC–MAX module is a real, nameable complex, and TRIM28 is genuinely placed in both diseases, so this clears the bar for a coherent, non-anatomically-obvious pairing. But the connection is not documented for this pair specifically: TFDP1, MXD1, MAZ and PAX8 return zero literature or Open Targets evidence in either disease, TRIM28's two disease-specific papers describe different sub-mechanisms (ERV silencing in IBS vs. NLRP3-linked proliferation in psoriasis), and IBS is not independently established as a hyperproliferative epithelial disorder the way psoriasis is.
support: PMID 39936987 — TRIM28 (with SETDB1) and aberrant endogenous retrovirus expression in IBS patients, placing TRIM28 in IBS mucosa but via ERV silencing, not the E2F/MYC-MAX arm. PMID 42720284 — TRIM28 promotes keratinocyte proliferation via an NLRP3/SGT1-linked axis in psoriasis, the one direct link from this factor list to psoriatic hyperproliferation.
how_to_falsify: In parallel organoid/keratinocyte models, knock down TFDP1 or overexpress MXD1 and measure EdU/BrdU incorporation and E2F target-gene expression against matched healthy tissue. If psoriatic keratinocytes show the expected proliferation shift but regenerating IBS mucosal epithelium (or an inflamed-IBS biopsy panel) shows no corresponding change in RB–E2F activity relative to controls, the gut side of the shared axis does not hold and the account is wrong.
caveats: Colorectal vs. skin tissue pairing across 32 patient-group comparisons drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so true replication is much narrower than the comparison count suggests. TCF3 topped this list (27/32) but its only literature hit (PMID 39073655) concerns E47 deficiency and agammaglobulinemia — pure B-lymphopoiesis, irrelevant to gut or skin — so it was excluded from the carrying set despite its rank. The MSC hits in the retrieved material (PMIDs 41480397, 40691643, 41571652, 41007656, 36925706) are about mesenchymal stem cell therapy, a cell type, not the musculin transcription factor MSC; this is a gene-symbol collision and was not used as TF evidence. PAX8 is thyroid-lineage-specific with no independent gut/skin biology behind it here — its inclusion rests entirely on shared target genes, not on any documented PAX8 role in either tissue. The single-view exclusions (NRF1, DNMT3L) and the tissue-generic filter don't bear directly on this module, but their removal is why no more generic proliferation regulator (e.g. a bare MYC or E2F1) appears in the list to anchor the story more strongly.
